ackKey.activate: I have saved the file — activate this key
ackKey.activated: The new key is active. The API now seals every delivery ack to it — make sure the tracker is flashed with the Config.h you just saved, or it will stop confirming deliveries.
ackKey.generate: Generate a new ack key pair
ackKey.insecureContext: Key generation needs a secure context. Open the dashboard over https (or on localhost), or mint the pair with openssl — the commands are in the file below.
ackKey.intro: With acks on, the tracker only clears a fix from its SD card once this API confirms the fix reached the database — a broker acknowledgement alone proves only that the broker took the message. The API seals each verdict to this device, so the device needs its own private key.
ackKey.leavingIsSafe: Leaving now costs nothing: the device keeps its current key and the server is untouched.
ackKey.stepActivate: Then activate the key here, which tells the API to start using its public half.
ackKey.stepSave: Download or copy the Config.h below — it now contains this private key.
ackKey.title: Delivery ack key
ackKey.unsavedTitle: Nothing has been saved yet. The private key below exists only in this page. Two steps remain:
ackKey.warning: Generating a new pair replaces the key this device uses. The tracker cannot read acks again until you flash it with the new Config.h, and the private key is shown once — it is never stored here or on the server, and cannot be recovered afterwards.

config.configCheckSleepNote: Deep sleep is on, so this setting does nothing. A sleeping tracker has no connection to re-check — it reads its configuration afresh on every wake, which already makes this redundant.

field.retryMaxAgeHours: Give up on rejected fixes after

config.fixTimeoutHint: A cold start under a poor sky view can legitimately take minutes. Too short and a parked car never reports; too long and a sleeping tracker burns the battery the sleep was meant to save.
config.fixTimeoutLabel: Give up on a lock after
config.intro: How often this tracker reports, whether it sleeps in between, and what it does with fixes it could not deliver. Changes are published to the broker, which holds them — so the device does not need to be online right now, and nothing has to be reflashed. An awake tracker applies a change within seconds; a sleeping one on its next wake.
config.outOfRange: "{{field}}" must be a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}.
config.queueMaxHint: While the broker is unreachable each fix is encrypted and queued on the SD card. Past this many, the oldest are dropped so the card can never fill up. It is a count rather than a duration because a queued entry is bare ciphertext with no timestamp to age it by.
config.rejectedHint: Fixes this server refused are kept apart from the live queue and re-offered slowly, because several reject reasons are server-side and clear on their own. Giving up is the only path that deliberately discards data.
config.scheduled: A schedule is in charge of these settings.
config.scheduledDetail: Saving here applies straight away, but the next profile switch replaces it. To change it for good, edit the profile in Settings › Schedule above.
config.scheduledWithProfile: A schedule is running the {{profile}} profile on this device.
config.sleepBetweenHint: Powers the modem down and reboots the tracker on wake. A large battery saving above roughly five minutes, but every cycle then pays for a cold GNSS fix and a fresh TLS handshake — below that it can cost more than it saves.
config.title: Reporting & Power
config.updatesHint: Settings normally reach this tracker within a second: it holds an open subscription, so the broker pushes a change the moment it is saved, and a device that reconnects is handed the current settings automatically. The value below is only the backstop — how often it asks the broker to re-send them, in case a connection was quietly dead.

danger.confirmPrompt: Are you sure? This cannot be undone.
danger.intro: Deleting the device deactivates it permanently for all users who have access. Historical position data is retained but no new positions will be accepted. This action cannot be undone.
danger.title: Danger Zone

firmware.intro: Everything the firmware is built with, read straight out of the file above. These are compile-time constants — changing one means editing Config.h and re-flashing. The reporting interval, sleep flag, GNSS timeout and queue limits are the exception: the values below are only the defaults a tracker falls back to, and Reporting & Power above is what actually sets them.

legend.secret: typed in above; never sent to the server

firmware.sectionIntro: A complete Config.h for this device — topics, broker URI, receiver public key and its current settings — ready to save and flash. Re-reading this is always safe: it re-renders the stored public key rather than generating a new pair, so a device already in the field keeps working.
firmware.title: Firmware Configuration

history.restored: Loaded those values into the form — review them, then save.

history.title: Version history

override.intro: This device is on a schedule, so saving here does not change what it runs from now on — it holds until the next scheduled switch, and then {{profile}} is applied again.
override.permanentDisable: Turn the schedule off, which leaves whatever you save here in force until somebody changes it.
override.permanentEditProfile: Edit the profile the schedule uses — in Settings Schedule above — so every future switch carries the new values; or
override.resumesNextSwitch: The schedule resumes at the next switch.
override.title: This change is temporary

provisioning.ackNotConfigured: Not configured — delivery acks are off
provisioning.copyFailed: Copying is not available here — download it, or select the text below.
provisioning.intro: A complete Config.h for this device — save it as ESP32/src/config/Config.h and run pio run. Everything specific to this tracker is already in it; the only blanks are the secrets below, which your browser fills in without sending them anywhere.
provisioning.keyNote: Only public keys appear above. The receiver private key — the one that decrypts positions — stays encrypted in the API database and never leaves the server, so neither this device nor the broker can read back its own positions. The ack private key is the mirror image: it is generated here, belongs to the device, and is never sent to the server.
provisioning.title: Firmware configuration

save.keptEdits: Refreshed around your edits — the values you typed were kept.
save.resumed: Schedule resumed — the scheduled profile is back in force.
save.savedPublished: Settings saved and published as v{{version}}. The device applies them on its next report.
save.savedTemporary: Saved as v{{version}}. These values hold until the next scheduled switch.

secrets.intro: These four values are the only blanks left in the file. They are inserted in this browser — they are never sent to the server, never stored, and are gone when you leave this page. Leave any of them empty and the file still builds; the matching feature just stays off.
secrets.mqttPasswordHint: The one you created for {{deviceId}} with mosquitto_passwd. The API does not issue broker accounts, so it cannot fill this in for you.
secrets.title: Your secrets
secrets.wifiSsidHint: Filling this in also switches kWifiEnabled on. Left empty, WiFi stays off so the tracker does not wait out a connect timeout on every boot.

diagram.synced: Settings have reached the device: dashboard, broker and device all confirmed.

explain.deepSleepWait: With deep sleep on it is only online briefly, so this can take up to one reporting interval ({{interval}}).
explain.pending: The broker is holding this change; the device applies it on its next report.
explain.synced: The settings below are the ones the tracker is using.
explain.unknown: Nothing is wrong with the settings — this device has simply never confirmed which revision it is running. Firmware older than remote settings never will.
